Gag Grouper Fishing From St. Pete in September 2026

Gag season is short this year. Get your gear ready for a decent weather window, with a few spots to try and enough time for the ride back.

By Catch 'N Bake · 3 minute read
Published September 14, 2026 · Updated September 14, 2026
Sources checked September 14, 2026. Check linked agencies for changes before fishing.

In this articleCheck the September 2026 gag seasonCheck the rules for where you dropPick a few spots you can workGet your release gear ready at the dockLeave time for a slower ride backPut the fish on ice and save the details

Check the September 2026 gag season

If you're trying to put a gag grouper in the cooler this September, get the boat and gear ready before the forecast lines up. For a trip from St. Pete, think through the run out and back when you're picking spots. Leave yourself enough time to fish once you get there.

2026 season check · September 14

FWC lists Gulf gag harvest as open September 1 through 30, 2026. NOAA lists the federal Gulf closure at 12:01 a.m. local time on October 1. Check both the FWC grouper rules and the NOAA season bulletin before your trip.

Check the year when somebody sends you a season announcement. Older gag dates still turn up in searches. For this trip, you need the Gulf rules for 2026.

Check the rules for where you drop

Figure out whether your spots are in state or federal waters before you leave the dock. Read the rules for those waters and any requirements that apply to your boat.

For Gulf gag, FWC lists a 24 inch total length minimum and two fish per person within the four grouper aggregate. Charter captain and crew have a zero gag bag limit. Check those limits alongside the season dates before the trip.

Booking a charter? Ask the captain where they expect to fish and what the plan is if the weather changes. Find out how a shorter trip or a different target species would affect your booking before you pay.

Pick a few spots you can work

If you need somewhere to start looking, pull up Pinellas County's artificial reef map. Pick a few locations that fit your boat, fuel range, and forecast. You'll still need to see what's happening when you get there.

Include the run through the pass when you plan the route. Have another spot you can try without adding a long ride to the day, and give boats already fishing the area plenty of room. Keep shipping channels clear.

On the spot, watch your line angle and whether you're staying in touch with the bottom. If you can't keep the bait where you want it, sort out the boat's position or your setup before sending down more bait.

Save the depth, rig, and bait you used. A reef name in your phone won't tell you how you fished it when you come back a month later.

Get your release gear ready at the dock

Put the measuring tool and dehooker where you can grab them. Set up your release gear before the first drop, even if you're heading out hoping for fish to keep.

FWC's Gulf reef fish gear rules cover circle hooks when using natural bait, dehooking equipment, and a descending device or venting tool rigged and ready. Check the section for your waters because the hook requirements differ between state and federal waters.

If you haven't used your release tool before, learn the setup ashore and keep the instructions handy. FWC's barotrauma guide explains why a fish brought up from depth may need help getting back down. Unpacking a new tool with a fish on deck is a bad time to figure it out.

Leave time for a slower ride back

Read the marine forecast for the water you plan to cross. The National Weather Service Tampa Bay office has forecasts, radar, and warnings. Check again before you leave.

Let somebody ashore know where you're headed and when you expect to return. Agree on a time to head in with the people on the boat. If the ride home could take longer than the run out, account for that before deciding to fish one more spot.

Put the fish on ice and save the details

Once you've confirmed a fish is legal to keep, get it cold and follow the landing requirements. Have a plan for cleaning it when you get back.

Our gag grouper taste and cooking guide has fillet preparation and dinner ideas. Before the day gets away from you, save a few notes on the catch. Include the depth, bait, and any adjustment you made before it ate.

Remember what worked.

Save your gag grouper photo and a few notes in Catch 'N Bake while the trip is fresh. When you bring a fish home, look up a recipe for it in the app. Get Catch 'N Bake on the App Store.
